feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Texas voters cast early ballots in key senate race
entry.summary: In Texas, early voting is underway. The state's tight race for U.S. Senate will ultimately help decide the balance of power in Washington.

entry.title: Protests roil France once again as police seek to quell violence
entry.summary: Hundreds of thousands turned out across France to protest everything from the lack of school funding to economic inequality. Police also were out in force to prevent a repeat of last week's violence.

entry.title: New memorial to the 1991 Gulf War opens
entry.summary: President Trump is weighing the possibility of another major attack on Iran. Today, just a few blocks from the White House, military veterans dedicated a memorial to an earlier Middle East conflict: the 1991 Gulf War, which was a military success, but is often overlooked.

entry.title: Chicago International Film Festival brings world cinema to the Windy City
entry.summary: The longest running competitive film festival in North America isn't in Los Angeles or New York, it's in Chicago. The Chicago International Film Festival marks its 62nd year.

entry.title: Comedian Charlie Berens has made Wisconsin politics a laughing matter
entry.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with comedian and former journalist Charlie Berens. His comedy blends political satire with a distinctly Wisconsin sense of humor.

entry.title: Trade tariffs cause whiplash at Port Milwaukee
entry.summary: Sacha Pfeiffer visits Port Milwaukee to see how President Trump's tariffs have affected the flow of goods and impacted the regional economy.

entry.title: 'Swing State of the Union' podcast digs deep on issues weighing on Wisconsin voters
entry.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Sam Woods and Joy Powers, hosts of WUWM's Swing State of the Union podcast, about the top issues for voters in the swing state of Wisconsin.

entry.title: How data centers became a bipartisan political issue in Wisconsin
entry.summary: Data centers are a big issue across the country. As midterms approach, many look to the swing state of Wisconsin for lessons for how that issue could play out nationally.

entry.title: Why a far-right cabinet minister in Israel has Netanyahu's ear
entry.summary: Israel's most far-right cabinet minister helped dictate hardline policies toward Palestinians in recent years. Benjamin Netanyahu vows to give him a senior position if Netanyahu is reelected next week.

entry.title: The latest in space science: We look back at the Big Bang
entry.summary: In this edition of Spacing Out, the team from Short Wave shares the latest developments in space science, including the theory on why the universe is made of matter
